title: DFS Pathfinding in Porto: Deep Dive to the Goal
description: We visualize DFS exploring Porto’s real street graph from start to finish, step by step. Watch how DFS dives deep into branches, backtracks, and eventually finds a path.
ig_caption:
🗺️✨ **DFS on a real Porto street map (Campanhã)**

In this visualization, **Depth-First Search (DFS)** treats intersections as **nodes** and street segments as **edges**, then commits to one route as deep as possible before backtracking. 🚶‍♂️🔁

🧠 **How DFS works (technical):**
- Uses a **stack (implicit via recursion or explicit data structure)** to track the next frontier.
- Marks visited nodes to prevent cycles—critical on dense road graphs.
- Depth-first behavior means it may find *a* valid path quickly, but **not always the shortest** (unless paired with specific conditions like limited depth or explored ordering).

📍 **Graph theory tie-in:** Porto’s streets form a large **undirected/directed graph** (depending on one-way rules). DFS navigates the graph by following adjacency lists, generating a traversal tree and backtracking when a branch dead-ends.

🚦📍 **DFS Pathfinding in Porto (Campanhã)**

Depth-First Search (DFS) is a graph search method that explores as far as possible along one path before backtracking. On real street maps, we model intersections as nodes and roads as edges, then DFS walks the graph using a stack and a visited set to avoid loops—building an implicit traversal tree as it goes.
